items.headline: It's list day — the 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees just dropped
items.body: Soccer's who's-the-best-on-the-planet debate officially opened Tuesday: the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d'Or is out, and it's a murderers' row — defending winner Ousmane Dembélé, teen sensation Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé, Lionel Messi, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane and Vinícius Júnior all made the cut. The winner gets crowned Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London.
items.say: The Ballon d'Or nominees came out today — that's the award for the single best soccer player in the world. Dembélé won it last year but that 19-year-old Lamine Yamal is right there. If you had a vote, who's your pick?

items.headline: Quarterfinal night in New York — and an American is guaranteed a spot in the semis
items.body: The US Open reaches the business end Tuesday, and it's a great night for the home crowd. Defending champ Carlos Alcaraz takes on big-serving American Ben Shelton under the lights at Arthur Ashe, and earlier the all-American clash between Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen guarantees at least one U.S. man in the semifinals — something that doesn't happen very often anymore.
items.say: The US Open quarterfinals are tonight — Alcaraz plays the American Ben Shelton, and there's an all-American match too, so we're locked into having a U.S. guy in the semis. Worth staying up for. You ever get sucked into the late-night matches?

items.headline: Team USA got the scare of the tournament — but escaped Italy 55-52
items.body: The mighty Americans nearly got shocked in Berlin. Italy hung with Team USA all night and even led inside the final four minutes before the U.S. gutted out a 55-52 win — the fewest points a U.S. women's team has scored since the three-point line arrived in 1984. Italy's Cecilia Zandalasini (14 points) had a look at a game-tying three in the closing seconds that just missed. The win still books the U.S. into the quarterfinals on Thursday.
items.say: Team USA at the Women's Basketball World Cup almost got upset by Italy — they scraped by 55-52, and Italy actually had a chance to tie it at the buzzer. For that team to nearly lose is wild. You catch any of it?

items.headline: Week 2 is stacked — a top-5 showdown and Oklahoma at Michigan
items.body: After a fun opening weekend, college football's second Saturday (Sept. 12) is loaded. The headliner is a top-5 heavyweight bout between Ohio State and Texas — both cruised through Week 1 — in the season's first clash of the giants. Add No. 10 Oklahoma visiting No. 16 Michigan in the noon Big Noon window, plus Oregon at Oklahoma State and the Cy-Hawk rivalry in primetime, and it's a full day on the couch.
items.say: College football's second week is a big one — Ohio State and Texas, two of the best teams in the country, go head to head, and Oklahoma's at Michigan too. Perfect all-day-on-the-couch Saturday. You pulling for anybody this fall?

items.headline: Football's back — and this week the NFL plays its first-ever game in Australia
items.body: The NFL season is finally here. It kicks off Wednesday night with a Super Bowl LX rematch — defending champion Seattle hosting New England — but the real novelty comes Thursday, when the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams face off at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in the first-ever NFL regular-season game played in Australia. Football, down under, at 8:30 in the morning Aussie fans' time? Wild.
items.say: The NFL's back this week, and get this — the Niners and Rams are actually playing a game in Australia, first time the league's ever done that. Fun way to start the season. You riding with a team this year?

items.headline: The witches are back — 'Practical Magic 2' casts its spell Friday
items.body: Nearly 30 years later, the Owens sisters return: 'Practical Magic 2' hits theaters Friday (Sept. 11), with Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman reprising the roles from the 1998 cult favorite. This time the next generation joins in — Maisie Williams and Joey King play their daughters — with Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest back too, as the family fights to break its old curse (yes, that midnight margarita energy is intact).
items.say: There's a Practical Magic sequel coming out Friday — Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman back as the witch sisters, almost 30 years after the first one. Total cozy-fall, girls'-night-in movie. You remember the original?

items.headline: The song that won't quit — Ella Langley makes chart history
items.body: If it feels like you've been hearing 'Choosin' Texas' forever, you're not wrong. Country breakout Ella Langley just notched a 20th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — the longest run ever for a non-holiday song, now trailing only Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' (22 weeks) for the all-time record. Not bad for a twangy heartbreak duet-turned-solo smash.
items.say: You know that song 'Choosin' Texas' by Ella Langley? It's been No. 1 for like 20 weeks straight — literally the longest a non-Christmas song has ever sat on top. Kind of insane. What's been stuck in your head lately?

links.text: Billboard — 20th week at No. 1, a new record

items.headline: Oscar season shifts to Toronto — and there's a Sylvester Stallone 'Rocky' movie
items.body: The fall awards race rolls into Canada as the Toronto International Film Festival runs Sept. 10-20 — famous as the launchpad where crowd-pleasers grab momentum (TIFF's audience award is a big Oscar bellwether). The buzziest title: Peter Farrelly's 'I Play Rocky,' a biopic about how Sylvester Stallone fought to make and star in the original 'Rocky.' Zack Snyder's 'The Last Photograph' premieres there too.
items.say: The Toronto Film Festival's kicking off — it's basically where the fall Oscar movies find their buzz. There's even a movie about how Stallone got 'Rocky' made against all odds. You into the awards-season films, or more of a blockbuster person?

items.headline: One last beach party — Sea.Hear.Now brings a stacked lineup to the Jersey Shore
items.body: The end-of-summer festival run peaks soon: Sea.Hear.Now takes over the Asbury Park beachfront Sept. 19-20 with a genuinely dad-and-coworker-friendly bill. Mumford & Sons headline Saturday and The Strokes close it out Sunday, with Pixies, Goo Goo Dolls, The Offspring, Fontaines D.C., The War on Drugs and Chaka Khan all along the sand. Music, ocean, boardwalk food — hard to beat.
items.say: There's a big music festival right on the beach in Asbury Park in a couple weeks — Mumford & Sons and The Strokes headlining, with the Pixies and Goo Goo Dolls too. Music on the sand sounds pretty perfect. You ever done a festival, or is that your nightmare?
